existing_solution_comparison: arXiv 2603.13252 'When Alpha Breaks' (abstract opened directly this session, claims deup2026_regime_trust_gate_definition, deup2026_epistemic_uncertainty_definition, deup2026_2024_regime_breakdown_motivation) is the published source: a LightGBM cross-sectional ranker at a 20-day horizon whose signal breaks in the 2024 AI-rally holdout, addressed by (1) a strategy-level regime-trust gate G(t) (AUROC ~0.72 overall, ~0.75 in the 2024 FINAL holdout) deciding whether to trade, and (2) a position-level epistemic tail-risk cap using a DEUP-style ehat (rank-displacement uncertainty) signal, found to correlate ~0.6 with absolute rank-score error -- explicitly NOT used as a continuous inverse-uncertainty sizing denominator because that de-levers the strongest signals and hurts performance (their own negative finding), hence their design uses ehat only as a tail-risk cap on the most uncertain names, matching this task's own candidate U3 design (drop the most-uncertain quintile, not continuous inverse scaling). No other implementation of this exact two-level DEUP framework was found in the repo's local prior art: `uv run oc research directions check` for 'uncertainty gate' and 'DEUP' both returned only this same registry row (dir:regime_trust_uncertainty_gate_momentum_ranker, status queued, likely_repeat 1.00 confirming it is this task's own queued entry, not a prior local result) and a grep of reports/research/{control,iterations,ledger} for 'deup|uncertainty gate|ensemble disagreement' found no prior local test of this mechanism (only this task's own queue block and the intel note that proposed it, I-20260928-03).
remaining_evidence_gap: The paper's abstract does not disclose its asset universe, cost model, training window, or the exact rank-displacement model behind ehat (methods section not independently opened -- abstract page only, paywalled/no separate PDF fetch attempted this session, disclosed as a limitation on every source-card row). No source found this session tests this two-level DEUP framework on a LONG-ONLY top-30 momentum book specifically, nor on this repo's own T1 20-session construction, nor whether a bootstrap-ensemble-standard-deviation proxy (this task's own operationalization of 'epistemic uncertainty', not the paper's own rank-displacement predictor) carries the same signal the paper reports. This is exactly the gap this iteration's own preregistered backtest is designed to close cheaply (AUROC/placebo stop conditions before any full G1-G5 run).

queries.query: When Alpha Breaks arXiv 2603.13252 regime-trust gate DEUP epistemic uncertainty cross-sectional ranker

sources.claim: The paper proposes a two-level deployment policy for a cross-sectional LightGBM ranker: a strategy-level regime-trust gate G(t) that decides whether to trade at all (AUROC around 0.72 overall and 0.75 in the 2024 FINAL holdout period), and a position-level epistemic tail-risk cap that reduces exposure only for the most uncertain individual predictions.
sources.market_and_period: Cross-sectional stock ranking (asset universe not disclosed in abstract), 20-day horizon, walk-forward, 2024 holdout ('FINAL period') coinciding with an AI thematic rally, 1,865 dates.
sources.applicability: Primary source and definition for this iteration's regime-trust-gate candidates U1/U2 and the DEUP-style individual-name cap U3; directly names the AUROC bar (0.72-0.75) this iteration's own 0.60 stop-condition threshold is set conservatively below.
sources.limitations: Abstract-only (methods section, exact G(t)/ehat model architecture, universe and costs not opened this session); AUROC numbers are the paper's own model/data, not a same-instrument replication.
sources.independent_replication: None found this session (2026 paper, too new); the paper's own reported regime break (LightGBM ranker weakens in the 2024 AI-rally holdout) independently corroborates this repo's own already-diagnosed problem (T1 momentum book 2024+ max drawdown -41.6% vs the -35% gate, docs/current-view.zh.md 2026-09-24 11:30 section) -- a different symptom of the same non-stationarity the paper describes, not a direct replication of its numbers.

sources.claim: The paper adapts Direct Epistemic Uncertainty Prediction (DEUP) to ranking by predicting rank displacement and defining an epistemic uncertainty signal ehat relative to a point-in-time-safe baseline; ehat's median correlation with absolute rank-score error is about 0.6 across 1,865 dates, and ehat is structurally coupled with signal strength, so naive inverse-uncertainty position sizing de-levers the strongest signals and degrades performance.
sources.applicability: Direct definition basis for this iteration's u_i(t) epistemic-uncertainty proxy (bootstrap ensemble standard deviation of cross-sectional rank predictions) and for choosing a tail-risk-cap design (U3: drop the most-uncertain quintile) over continuous inverse-uncertainty sizing, matching the paper's own negative finding about naive inverse sizing.
sources.limitations: Exact ehat construction (the rank-displacement predictor's own architecture/training) is in the paper's methods section, not opened this session; this iteration's ensemble-standard-deviation proxy is a standard, disclosed simplification, not a literal reimplementation.
sources.independent_replication: None found this session (too new); internally consistent with the standard ensemble-disagreement-as-epistemic-uncertainty literature (not separately re-verified this session, out of scope for a same-day abstract read).

sources.claim: In the paper's own 'AI Stock Forecaster' setting, a LightGBM cross-sectional ranker performs well overall at a 20-day horizon, but the 2024 holdout period coincides with an AI thematic rally and sector rotation that breaks the signal at longer horizons and weakens the 20-day signal specifically.
sources.applicability: Independent corroboration, named in the registry row, for why this repo's own 2024+ momentum-book drawdown might be addressable by a trained confidence signal rather than a fixed rule (which already failed, H-20260924-02).
sources.limitations: Universe, exact AI-rotation dates and cost model not disclosed in the abstract; motivational evidence, not a transferable number.
sources.independent_replication: Consistent with this repo's own T1 book reproduction (run_h20260924_02_momentum_crash_guard.py), which shows a real 2024+ drawdown in the same calendar period.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Train k=15 bootstrap LightGBM regressors walk-forward (expanding window, annual retrain, purge>=21 sessions) on rank-normalized kt.BASE_FEATURE_COLUMNS for the top-500 universe; compute u_i(t) ensemble disagreement and book-level U(t)/z(t); apply candidates U1/U2/U3 to the unchanged T1 book; check AUROC and the two placebo/owner-rule stop conditions on the 2024-01-08..latest window before any stress-window or G1-G5 work.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: At least one candidate clears (a) AUROC>=0.60 where applicable, (b) beats its own placebo distribution on both the drawdown-improvement and Sharpe checks, and (c) anchor-window Sharpe >= vol-matched-control Sharpe + 0.10.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: No candidate clears all of (a)/(b)/(c) on the anchor window -- refuted at stage 1, no stress-window or G1-G5 work performed, registry row updated to refuted with the exact numbers.
